prediction_question: Given everything documented about a mine and its own prior inspections and citations before an inspection begins, which of the declared set of 30 CFR sections will MSHA cite at this inspection?
prediction_time: The instant the inspection begins (INSPECTION_BEGIN_DT). Every feature is either a static mine attribute (Mines table), the inspection's own trigger recorded when it opens (ACTIVITY_CODE/ACTIVITY, PROGRAM_AREA, INSPECT_OFFICE_CD), or a field of an earlier inspection of the same MINE_ID. Everything the inspector observes or records during the visit is post-hoc and excluded.
target_definition: The set of 30 CFR sections cited at one inspection (EVENT_NO), i.e. the distinct PART_SECTION values of its violation rows - multi-label, mean 5.79 sections per inspection, median 2. The raw label space is 5,934 sections; construction declares a floor (104 sections at >= 1% of inspections, 183 at >= 0.5%). PART_SECTION itself and every violation-level attribute of the cited rows are excluded from the shipped features.

license_decision: DECIDED 2026-10-12 (operator, option A): treat US federal government works as public domain for this source, record the reasoning and proceed to construction; explicit written permission is NOT sought. MSHA states no terms (data-set pages and definition file are silent; the data.gov entry carries accessLevel=public and rights="true" and names no licence), so the basis is statutory - 17 USC 105 - and no publisher grant is claimed. Two third parties already redistribute derived MSHA data (CC0; CC-BY-4.0 via Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20572372); the operator weighed that as precedent, not as permission. Recorded in candidates/msha-enforcement-citations/license.json, from which release-manifest.py builds the release's licenses block. Reversal point: if MSHA publishes terms, or the operator narrows this decision, the change lands in that file alone.
construction_script: candidates/msha-enforcement-citations/source/build.py (streaming build; one binary config per floor 30 CFR section) plus source/run.sh (worker entrypoint: entrypoint script streams the three MSHA zips, builds, qualifies every config on the worker). Both bundled into the worker image - the artifact's manifest records their sha256, and msha-002's bundled build.py hash equals the committed file.
split_strategy: Temporal by inspection year, no random component, three disjoint windows: train 2001-2020 (415,088 inspections / 2,459,741 citations), eval 2021-2023 (49,233 / 255,952), holdout 2024-2025 (33,576 / 175,151). The probe checked that every one of the 104 sections it measured at >= 1% of the full inspection census occurs in every window; construction recomputes the floor on its constructed pool (497,897 events, 80 sections at >= 1% of the pool) and ships the 45 highest-prevalence of those - see qualification.floor. 2000 (19,640 inspections) is the earliest full year and folds into train; 2026 is partial and is not used.

novelty_check.theirs: MSHA ships the raw tables, the definition files, MDRS and descriptive calculators (S&S rate, pattern of violations), but no prediction task and no splits. Mine-safety ML prior art predicts accidents/injuries or violation counts, or which mines to inspect (binary targeting): Univ. of Kentucky thesis 'Temporal Machine Learning for Predicting Accidents and Violations at Surface Coal Mines', 'Machine Learning Classification Models for More Effective Mine Safety Inspections', Marshall's random-forest pattern study, and the ASCE-ASME J. Risk enforcement-action study. OSHA-side work is establishment targeting, not a cited-standard set. Two Hugging Face artifacts that mention MSHA were opened and read on 2026-09-27 and neither is this task: emperor-mew/msha-violations is a dataset card with no data files (it points at a live REST API for citation-level records), and FastDOLz/msha-mine-safety-violations-by-operator is operator-level aggregation (40,720 operators, 3,076,282 violations rolled up with penalty totals and cross-agency OSHA/WHD indicators, CC-BY-4.0, Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20572372). No package ships the inspection-level multi-label set of cited sections with a prediction instant and splits.
novelty_check.ours: The multi-label formulation itself: one row per MSHA inspection, target = the set of 30 CFR sections cited at that inspection (104 sections at a >=1% floor, 183 at >=0.5%), with an explicit prediction instant at INSPECTION_BEGIN_DT, a pre-inspection-only feature set drawn from the Mines table plus the mine's own inspection and citation history, and three disjoint temporal windows (2001-2020 / 2021-2023 / 2024-2025) each holding every floor label. No ML-ready package ships this task.
novelty_check.rule: A dataset that already exists in ML-ready form is not published. Mirroring is a failure mode, not a contribution.
